inspection_summary: The complete retained 101-line, three-page preview was inspected. Its usable prose moves from an ancient view of Number as foundational, through a contrast between final-theory aspirations and the apparent open-endedness of number theory, to a literary encounter with indivisibility, an explicit factorization-based account of primality, a compressed history of primes before and in Euclid, and the claim that established results continually generate heuristics and open questions. Page furniture interrupts two sentences, but the prose continuity is recoverable; this assessment is limited to the retained preview and makes no claim about the unseen book.

accepted_units.title: Number as a proposed architecture of reality
accepted_units.why_material: The passage supplies a historically situated semantic viewpoint in which Number is not merely a collection of objects but a candidate organizing principle more basic than material constituents, and it immediately turns that viewpoint into an open question about the maturity of numerical understanding.
accepted_units.context_note: The claim is explicitly attributed to Aristotle's report about early Pythagoreans and should remain historical-philosophical framing rather than a mathematical theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Recoverable from continuous prose and a short quotation; no formula, image, or external context is required.

accepted_units.title: Final-theory aspiration contrasted with inexhaustible number theory
accepted_units.why_material: The text juxtaposes Descartes' hope that geometry was nearly exhausted and modern physicists' final-theory aspiration with the opposite strategic expectation for pure number theory: great existing power does not imply conceptual completion, and unexplored depth may be unbounded.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 21-23 continue only at line 41 after a page break, running header, image caption, and publication footer; both sides are necessary to recover the comparison.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on reconnecting prose split by extraction/page furniture at lines 24-40; no mathematical notation is involved.

accepted_units.title: A composition constraint exposes resistance to division
accepted_units.why_material: The Don Quixote episode turns primality into an experienced obstruction: a fixed total cannot be arranged into the proposed equal stanza patterns without excess or deficit, and the demand that it nevertheless fit dramatizes the difference between willing a decomposition and one structurally existing.
accepted_units.context_note: The literary example is motivational rather than a proof and uses the source's concrete count only to exhibit the stated divisibility obstruction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the prose description of acrostic and stanza-layout constraints; the stated surplus and deficit are taken from the source, with no hidden computation required.

accepted_units.title: Primality reframed as failure of factorization
accepted_units.why_material: The passage converts the preceding divisibility difficulty into the structural definition that a prime cannot be expressed as a product of smaller numbers, then illustrates how such a property might be invoked to explain a natural cycle.
accepted_units.context_note: The cicada connection is explicitly hedged by the authors ('people tell us') and should be retained as an anecdotal proposed application, not as an established causal result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Plain prose centered on factorization; it contains a concrete prime example but no formula-dependent reasoning.

accepted_units.title: From sparse pre-Euclidean notice to the composite/incomposite distinction
accepted_units.why_material: The passage distinguishes a concept's later foundational status from its uneven early textual visibility, identifies the composite/incomposite contrast as a conceptual lens for priority, and locates Euclid as the point at which primes enter the preserved mathematical record in earnest.
accepted_units.context_note: The sentence begun at lines 60-64 resumes at lines 85-90 after footnotes, publication furniture, a page change, and an image caption; the entire span is required for coherent historical continuity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on reconnecting prose across extraction furniture at lines 65-84 and on preserving attribution; no unreadable mathematics or imported historical facts are needed.

accepted_units.title: Each discovery enlarges the space of questions
accepted_units.why_material: Rather than portraying established truths as closure, the passage presents them as productive inputs to further educated guesses, heuristics, expectations, and unsolved problems, a reusable account of how mathematical knowledge redirects search.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a general methodological claim about whole numbers and primes, not a specific theorem or evidence for any particular conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Continuous prose; no dependence on formulas, images, or adjacent unseen pages.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Foundational ambition without epistemic closure
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The preview links a strong claim about Number's organizing importance to an anti-finality stance: mathematical importance does not entail that the subject is near completion, because established truths can enlarge rather than contract the space of strategic questions.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a synthesis of philosophical and methodological framing in the preview, not a formal claim about the Riemann Hypothesis or evidence about the unseen remainder of the book.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From encountered obstruction to an explicit mathematical class
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A failed attempt to impose an equal-part composition makes indivisibility experientially salient; factorization then compresses that obstruction into a definition, while the historical passage shows the resulting class becoming explicit and mathematically central.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The literary example and compressed historical report illustrate a conceptual transition; they do not establish a theorem about prime distribution, and the natural-cycle remark remains hedged.
